docs.title: godolt
docs.text:
godolt wraps Dolt's operational surface for Go programs, following the gogit precedent — a standalone, dependency-light service-integration module.

Design: SQL-first. The primary workload is many concurrent sessions against dolt sql-server (the embedded driver sustains only one stable connection and is not a target), so version-control verbs run as Dolt stored procedures over the same MySQL wire as queries. The caller supplies the *sql.DB and godolt adds zero driver dependencies. The few operations that cannot run over the wire — clone/init bootstrap, server lifecycle, backups — shell out to the dolt CLI.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
• Client — New(db *sql.DB) wraps an existing *sql.DB connection to a dolt sql-server; the caller owns the driver, pooling, and DSN.
  • Remotes — Client.RemoteAdd, Client.RemoteRemove, and Client.Remotes register, remove, and list configured remotes (CALL DOLT_REMOTE(...)).
  • Sync — Client.Push and Client.Fetch push/fetch against a remote (CALL DOLT_PUSH/DOLT_FETCH), returning the server's status message. Push is fast-forward-only; a diverged remote rejects it. Client.Pull fetches and merges a remote's branch (CALL DOLT_PULL), returning *PullResult (FastForward, Conflicts, Message) — a non-zero Conflicts means the merge completed but left conflict rows in dolt_conflicts_<table> for the caller to resolve locally.
  • Branch — Client.ActiveBranch returns the connection's active branch (SELECT active_branch()).
  • Bootstrap — Clone(ctx, remoteURL, dir) and InitDir(ctx, dir, name, email) are cold-path operations that shell out to the dolt CLI, since no server exists yet to talk to.
  • Availability — Available() reports whether the dolt CLI is on PATH, the cold path's prerequisite.
  • Backups — BackupAdd, BackupSync, and BackupRestore manage named backup targets, snapshot/sync, and restore. No DOLT_BACKUP stored procedure exists, so these are CLI-exec only — verified safe to run against a directory a live dolt sql-server is actively serving.
db, _ := sql.Open("mysql", "root:@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/mydb")
client := godolt.New(db)

if err := client.RemoteAdd(ctx, "origin", "file:///path/to/remote"); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
msg, err := client.Push(ctx, "origin", "main")

Install:

go get github.com/grokify/godolt

See the README for full usage examples, and Releases for version history.

docs.title: godolt v0.1.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-08-16

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: godolt wraps Dolt's operational surface for Go programs, following the gogit precedent — a standalone, dependency-light service-integration module. This is the initial release: a SQL-wire client for the primary workload (many concurrent sessions against dolt sql-server), plus CLI-exec operations for the cold path (bootstrap, before a server exists) and backups (no SQL-callable equivalent exists).

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• SQL-wire Client for remotes, push/pull/fetch, and active branch — zero added driver dependencies, the caller supplies the *sql.DB
  • CLI-exec bootstrap (Clone, InitDir) and backup (BackupAdd, BackupSync, BackupRestore) operations for the cold path

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/godolt@v0.1.0

docs.title: SQL-wire client (the primary workload)
docs.text:
• New(db *sql.DB) *Client — wraps an existing connection to a dolt sql-server; the caller owns the driver, pooling, and DSN
  • Client.RemoteAdd, Client.RemoteRemove, Client.Remotes — register, remove, and list configured remotes via CALL DOLT_REMOTE(...)
  • Client.Push, Client.Pull, Client.Fetch — sync against a remote via CALL DOLT_PUSH/DOLT_PULL/DOLT_FETCH, returning the server's status message
  • Client.ActiveBranch — the connection's active branch via SELECT active_branch()
  • Argument validation (quotable) rejects characters that could escape a single-quoted SQL literal, since Dolt stored procedures don't support placeholders in all versions

docs.title: CLI-exec cold path
docs.text:
• Clone(ctx, remoteURL, dir) — clone a remote into a fresh directory
  • InitDir(ctx, dir, name, email) — initialize a new Dolt database directory with a committer identity
  • Available() — reports whether the dolt CLI is on PATH
  • BackupAdd, BackupSync, BackupRestore — named backup targets, snapshot/sync, and restore (--force to overwrite an existing restore directory); no DOLT_BACKUP stored procedure exists, so these are CLI-exec only. Verified safe to run against a directory a live dolt sql-server is actively serving

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Multi-tenant services — many concurrent sessions against a shared dolt sql-server, without an embedded-driver bottleneck
  • Service bootstrap — initialize or clone a Dolt database directory before a server exists to connect to
  • Operational backups — schedule backup sync against a live server without stopping it first

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• README with installation, usage examples, and a full API reference table
  • MIT license
  • README badges for CI, lint, SAST, godoc, MkDocs, visualization, and license status

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
• Shared CI workflows: Go CI (test matrix across Linux/macOS/Windows), Go Lint (golangci-lint), Go SAST (CodeQL), and Dependabot config
  • .gitignore for MkDocs build output and local env files

docs.title: godolt v0.2.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-08-17

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A single fix release: Client.Pull was broken on every call since v0.1.0. CALL DOLT_PULL returns a three-column result (fast_forward, conflicts, message) — a different shape from every other stored procedure godolt's shared call() helper handles (one or two columns) — so Pull unconditionally errored with sql: expected 3 destination arguments in Scan, not 2, regardless of whether the pull itself would have succeeded. Found while building VisionStudio's cloud-to-local sync (RMI-VISIONSTUDIO-535) and verified against a real dolt sql-server reproducing true history divergence before and after the fix.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: • Client.Pull's return type changes from (string, error) to (*PullResult, error). There is no compatible old signature to preserve: every caller of the v0.1.0 Pull was receiving a Go error on every invocation, so nothing depended on the old (broken) return shape in practice.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Client.Pull now scans DOLT_PULL's actual (fast_forward, conflicts, message) result directly instead of going through call()'s 1-or-2-column assumption. The new PullResult{FastForward, Conflicts, Message} surfaces the conflict count rather than silently mis-parsing or swallowing it — a non-zero Conflicts is not treated as an error, since the merge completed and left resolvable conflict rows in dolt_conflicts_<table> for the caller.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/godolt@v0.2.0

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Reproduced true history divergence — two independent clones each committing before either syncs the other's push, not just an unpushed local commit — against a real dolt sql-server:

  • The second push is genuinely non-fast-forward; Dolt's own remote logic rejects it (... [rejected] ... (non-fast-forward)), confirming push was already fast-forward-only by design before this fix.
  • Client.Pull on the rejected side now succeeds, merges cleanly, and reports Conflicts: 0 for the divergent-but-non-conflicting case.
  • A subsequent push from the same client succeeds once the pull has integrated the remote's history.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• README's Sync feature row split to describe Pull's new return shape separately from Push/Fetch; usage example extended with a Pull call and conflict check
  • MkDocs site Sync description updated to match
